All 88 tests pass (100%). The only excluded ones (`test-alt-string`, `cmake_fetch_content`) fail on the unmodified baseline too — unrelated to this fix.

## Summary of the fix

The enum `to_json` overload in include/nlohmann/detail/conversions/to_json.hpp:1656 always cast to the underlying type and stored it as `number_integer`. I changed it to check whether the enum's underlying type is unsigned:

```cpp
using underlying_type = typename std::underlying_type<EnumType>::type;
using cast_type = typename std::conditional<std::is_unsigned<underlying_type>::value,
                      typename BasicJsonType::number_unsigned_t,
                      typename BasicJsonType::number_integer_t>::type;
external_constructor<std::is_unsigned<underlying_type>::value ? value_t::number_unsigned : value_t::number_integer>::construct(j, static_cast<cast_type>(e));
```

This is C++11-compatible (no `if constexpr` needed). Applied the same change to `single_include/nlohmann/json.hpp:5700`.

Verification:
- Standalone repro compiles and passes on C++11/14/17/2a: `json(book_id(1ULL << 63))` is now `number_unsigned`, dumps as `"9223372036854775808"`, and signed enums still serialize as negative integers.
- Full unit test suite in the container: 88/88 tests pass, including `test-udt` (70 assertions, up from 64 — the new unsigned-enum checks all pass).
